problem_text:
A municipality aims to devise a stormwater runoff reduction strategy to lower sediment discharge from several construction sites across the city. Initially, no mitigation practices are in place.

The sediment generation profile for each site is as follows:
* For Site A, sediment coefficient is 0.836, site activity level is 255.992.
* For Site B, sediment coefficient is 2.936, site activity level is 235.236.
* For Site C, sediment coefficient is 1.608, site activity level is 239.873.
* For Site D, sediment coefficient is 2.565, site activity level is 266.797.
* For Site E, sediment coefficient is 1.174, site activity level is 255.254.
* For Site F, sediment coefficient is 1.542, site activity level is 178.817.
* For Site G, sediment coefficient is 2.114, site activity level is 89.743.
* For Site H, sediment coefficient is 0.97, site activity level is 127.781.
* For Site I, sediment coefficient is 1.028, site activity level is 176.699.

To manage discharge, several best management practices (BMPs) are available, each with a specific capture rate:
* Implementing BMP1 captures 79% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP2 captures 22% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP3 captures 20% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP4 captures 88% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP5 captures 75% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP6 captures 23% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP7 captures 23% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP8 captures 70% of sediment.
* Implementing BMP9 captures 53% of sediment.

Deploying a BMP at a site incurs a unit cost per activity level. The cost matrix for all site–BMP pairings is provided below:

| Site \ BMP | BMP1 | BMP2 | BMP3 | BMP4 | BMP5 | BMP6 | BMP7 | BMP8 | BMP9 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Site A | 184.426 | 143.88 | 62.056 | 166.466 | 105.974 | 130.728 | 33.536 | 15.807 | 80.769 |
| Site B | 122.868 | 43.741 | 175.391 | 121.507 | 76.454 | 41.068 | 179.953 | 152.303 | 140.882 |
| Site C | 64.163 | 83.447 | 40.952 | 118.729 | 193.334 | 172.851 | 133.002 | 138.762 | 61.126 |
| Site D | 87.806 | 13.81 | 158.258 | 155.839 | 11.691 | 183.188 | 133.001 | 124.217 | 11.608 |
| Site E | 57.954 | 162.966 | 68.037 | 193.735 | 132.121 | 90.523 | 81.53 | 76.255 | 57.88 |
| Site F | 98.673 | 138.667 | 166.619 | 85.459 | 29.439 | 107.188 | 135.848 | 170.224 | 81.104 |
| Site G | 132.995 | 125.72 | 66.71 | 30.54 | 22.129 | 197.789 | 131.713 | 173.683 | 59.618 |
| Site H | 145.108 | 179.551 | 66.77 | 38.487 | 155.44 | 180.941 | 163.032 | 162.449 | 124.006 |
| Site I | 135.501 | 139.344 | 147.044 | 134.526 | 199.519 | 59.291 | 89.527 | 83.772 | 16.711 |

The municipality must decide which BMPs to apply at each site (sites may employ multiple BMPs concurrently), and a site may also remain partially untreated if needed. The objective is to guarantee that the total sediment discharge is lowered by at least a fraction P = 0.554 of the baseline amount, while minimizing the total implementation cost.
